thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall — Severity 2: streaming tail latency spike observed for model redwood-alpha-1 in us-west-2.
ajay: saw alerts from latency-dashboard — p95 = 750ms, p99 = 3.8s for streaming endpoints. Spike ~10:12 UTC
maria: noticing many streaming sessions stuck in 'waiting-for-kv' state, KV cache miss rate jumped from 4%->22%
ajay: correlating with infra metrics now, checking GPU telemetry
infra-bot: node gpu-node-8 (ip:10.1.16.8) reported: correctable_ecc_count +490 in last 10m; fan_rpm dropped ~25% over 8m; power_draw spiking; temp_peak = 92C
jules: wow, that's high. Has the node started thermal-throttling? any kernel logs?
ajay: grabbing dmesg, tail:
```
[ 2134.123456] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00:00: Temperature threshold exceeded
[ 2134.123457] NVRM: GPU has been throttled due to thermal event
[ 2134.123460] nvidia: Correctable ECC error detected on GDDR6
```
maria: streaming worker logs show repeated KV cache stall on shard s-12 hitting GPU 3 on that node; latency correlates per trace id
support-esc: any customer impact yet? which accounts saw errors/timeouts?
ajay: anomaly detection shows ~1.9% of active streaming sessions experienced >2s stalls; highest impact on customers: acme-ads (10 calls), medboard (4 calls) — support escalation opened: INC-310246
jules: immediate mitigation: route stream traffic off gpu-node-8 to fallback pool and enable model fallback to redwood-alpha-1-quantized for new sessions
ajay: started routing rule change via runtime-router: `route modify --node=10.1.16.8 --weight=0 --drain=true` — applying now
infra-bot: routing change committed; new sessions will avoid node within 12s; existing KV-cache owners still on node
maria: can we force migrate long-lived sessions? streaming client continuity concerns
jules: migrate sessions slowly: `migrate-stream --shard s-12 --max-inflight=5` — avoid mass reconnect
ajay: migration started, throttled to avoid client drop; watching p99
support-esc: pinging impacted customers with a short note — ETA for full mitigation?
jules: short-term: node cordon + move shards = 10-20m; long-term: hardware replacement after root cause
ajay: monitoring: p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 1.1s after routing change; p95 stable at ~600ms
maria: ECC correctable counts still increasing, suggests flaky memory or VRAM degradation; fan rpm recovery intermittent
infra-bot: recommended action: increase fan target via BMC; also run nvme/firmware sanity? open ticket with datacenter: DC-4571
jules: oncall handoff — taking over. @jules is now primary on-call for incident. Timeline notes to incident doc INC-310246
jules: next steps: 1) cordon gpu-node-8 2) drain remaining workers 3) schedule hardware swap with on-site tech 4) run extended memtest on replacement node
ajay: cordon command executed: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-8` — pods evicted gradually
maria: drain in progress, 18/22 streaming pods migrated, 4 still moving; no client disconnect spikes so far
support-esc: update sent to customers: We're experiencing tail latency on streaming in us-west-2; we're routing traffic away from a degraded GPU node. Engineering is working on a hardware-level mitigation. No request data lost.
incident-bot: Incident INC-310246 created; sev:2; responder: jules; runbook: gpu-thermal-throttle
jules: after drain complete will confirm metrics stable for 15m before closing active page; will coordinate hardware ticket
infra-bot: created DC ticket DC-4571 for on-site tech — request: check fan assembly, replace riser, run memtest; ETA 6h
ajay: capturing traces for postmortem: collected sample_ids: [smp-310246-a1,smp-310246-b4] and KV cache hit/miss histograms
maria: prepping postmortem notes: suspected sequence — gradual fan rpm drop -> temp rise -> correctable ECC burst -> thermal throttle -> KV stalls -> p99 tail spike
support-esc: customers acknowledged. No billing credits requested yet, will escalate if SLA hit
jules: final check: p99 now at 420ms over 5m window, p95 580ms. I'll leave a follow-up action to validate firmware and schedule preventive replacements
ajay: thanks everyone — handing to jules for next steps, monitoring remains on
jules: copying to runbook and closing active page in 30m if stable :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Active mitigation complete. Follow-ups: postmortem, DC swap, firmware audit. Closing page in 30m if no regression.
